title: A design can be SKIPPED: the aggregate records the skip and the decoder refuses a half-skipped revision
description:
SPIDR prerequisite of task-de0598236f3b4d95aa3b6098b9d56995 (architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05), cut on the DATA axis. That row measured at ~10 distinct files with two of them already at or over the per-file cap; this row carries the one piece that had no home at all.

HUMAN DECISION, 2026-09-05, taken in the REPL after the architect measured that the toggle had no precedent (`git grep -ln 'skipDesign|GoalSettings|perGoal' -- apps/daemon/src` = ZERO hits) and that its obvious home was closed: `goal.create`'s payload is exact-arity `["instructions","title"]` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:295), so widening it is a separate multi-file roster job on the critical path. The human chose: RECORD THE SKIP ON THE EXISTING DESIGN AGGREGATE. No new command kind, no new aggregate, no vocabulary or registry backfill. The alternatives considered and rejected were widening `goal.create` (roster job) and a project-level flag (would have forced DoD-6 of the parent to be rewritten from "per-goal" to "per-project").

OBJECTIVE: make "this goal plans without a design" a durable, readable fact on `design:<goalId>`.

DELIVERABLE WHEN DONE: a design revision can carry a SKIPPED marker; `designRead` answers it; and a revision that is half-skipped - marked skipped while still carrying sections, or marked un-skipped while carrying none - is REFUSED with a stable code and its layer.

MEASURED AT HEAD f3b94eaa (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-b63fabf3:
- `apps/daemon/src/design/` holds 9 files landed by task-5e90317e (DONE, sha 34baaf52, reviewed: 48 tests, three drills). This row extends that contract; it does not rewrite it.
- `design-contracts.ts:39` `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` = `["apiSurface","componentList","dataModel","nonFunctional","openDecisions","screens"]` - SIX keys, `/** Sorted, and compared by exact arity. */`.
- `design-contracts.ts:44` `DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS` = the FIVE sections, `/** named apart from openDecisions so a dropped one names itself */`.
- `exactDesignRecord` at :150 and `decodeDesignRevision` at :232 are the arity gate. `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` at :65 is the closed code->layer map; `designRefusal` at :120 takes the CODE only and reads the layer from that map, so a call site structurally cannot mint a disagreeing pair. Use it; never pass a layer literal.
- THE BLAST RADIUS IS CONTAINED AND MEASURED: `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions' -- . ':!.moe'` returns exactly FOUR files, all under apps/daemon/src/design/ - design-contracts.ts, design-contracts.test.ts, design-store.test.ts, design-test-fixtures.ts. Nothing outside that directory names the revision keys.
- `design-records.ts:31` `DESIGN_RECORD_KEYS` does NOT mirror the revision keys (`revision` is one key), so the RECORD shape is untouched by this row.
- `design.submit` / `design.read` are NOT yet published on any command roster (`git grep -n 'design\.submit|design\.read'` hits only design-store.ts:155, a record field). That publication is task-06ac0da1's and this row does NOT need it: this row changes a decoder and its aggregate, not a wire.

THE HAZARD THAT DEFINES THIS ROW: `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` is compared by EXACT ARITY. Adding a seventh key makes every existing six-key revision payload REFUSE - every fixture, every test arm, every future caller. That is not a side effect to absorb quietly; it is the main event. Either the new key is genuinely required on every revision (and all four files move together in one commit), or the decode admits both arities deliberately and a test pins WHICH. Decide it at plan time, say which in the completion record, and drill it: a six-key revision must still round-trip, or must refuse with a named code - never silently.

NOT IN SCOPE - owned by named rows:
- The affordance surface reading this marker to skip the step - the successor row filed alongside this one.
- The wrapper staffing a design seat, and any mission text - task-de0598236f3b4d95aa3b6098b9d56995.
- Publishing `design.submit`/`design.read` on the command roster or over MCP - task-06ac0da1 and task-7f9f20c7.
- Any UI - task-8a6d6660's child 3.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src/design` (the shape task-5e90317e used and QA reproduced; `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 48 passed (48)` was its baseline). Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck` and quote their count lines.
definitionOfDone: A design revision can be marked SKIPPED on the `design:<goalId>` aggregate, and `designRead` answers that marker distinguishably from both "no design has ever been submitted" and "a real design exists". Assert all THREE states against a real store built by the production journey (the pattern task-5e90317e used), not against a hand-built fixture object - a two-state assertion cannot tell a skip from an absent read, which is the exact confusion this row exists to remove.

The arity decision is MADE, PINNED and DRILLED. `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` is compared by exact arity (design-contracts.ts:39 comment, enforced at `exactDesignRecord`:150), so a seventh key changes what every existing payload decodes to. State in the completion record which rule you chose - required-on-every-revision, or both arities admitted - and pin it with a test that asserts a SIX-key revision's outcome by name (round-trips, or refuses with a specific code). `expect(result.ok).toBe(false)` alone does not satisfy this clause.

A HALF-SKIPPED revision is refused with a stable code AND its layer asserted: marked skipped while still carrying sections, and marked un-skipped while carrying no sections. The code comes through `designRefusal(<code>)` so the layer is read from `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` (design-contracts.ts:65) - a layer string literal at any throw site is a defect, because `designRefusal` accepts no layer argument precisely so no call site can mint a disagreeing pair. If a NEW code is added, it joins that closed map and `DESIGN_CODES` derives from the map's keys, never from a second hand-written list.

All four measured consumers move in the SAME commit and none is left decoding the old arity: apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.ts, design-contracts.test.ts, design-store.test.ts, design-test-fixtures.ts. Re-run `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions' -- . ':!.moe'` at the delivered tree and confirm it still returns exactly those four - a fifth consumer appearing mid-flight is a stop-and-report, not an extra path to take.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line, restored and proved: flip the skipped/sections consistency check so a half-skipped revision is admitted, and confirm the arm from DoD-3 goes RED naming the code (not merely "threw"). `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST; every file here is TRACKED so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof, in a call SEPARATE from the restore - say so explicitly rather than leaving global rail 13 unaddressed.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src/design`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence here and must not be quoted as such - vitest.config.ts:32 includes no `apps/**`, so it runs zero tests against this row's files. Attribute any foreign red by the merge-base/HEAD failing-path delta intersected with apps/daemon/src/design/.
taskRails: DATA SHAPE ONLY, INSIDE apps/daemon/src/design/. This row publishes no command kind, offers no affordance step, staffs no seat and writes no mission text. If a step needs the surface or the wrapper to be meaningful, it belongs to a successor row - say so and move on.

EXACT ARITY IS THE POINT, NOT AN OBSTACLE. `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` is compared by arity, so a seventh key redefines every existing payload's outcome. Do not work around it by loosening `exactDesignRecord` for everything - that would silently admit unknown keys on every design and delete the guarantee task-5e90317e shipped.

REFUSALS COME THROUGH `designRefusal(<code>)`, which reads the layer from the closed `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` map and accepts no layer argument. A layer string literal at a throw site is a defect even when it happens to be the right string.

This row EXTENDS a DONE row's contract (task-5e90317e, sha 34baaf52). Read its reviewSummary before editing: three drills and 48 tests already guard this directory. Do not delete or weaken an existing arm to make a new one fit.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. (a) THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION UNDERCOUNTS ITS OWN BLAST RADIUS - correct it before you plan around it. The description says "exactly FOUR files", which was a grep of the KEY ROSTERS (`DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions`). The TYPE `DesignRevision` has consumers those rosters do not name. Run BOTH greps: `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions' -- . ':!.moe'` AND `git grep -n 'DesignRevision\b' -- . ':!.moe'`. A SIXTH file outside apps/daemon/src/design/ is a stop-and-report. (b) CONFIRM THE CONTRACT IS UNTOUCHED SINCE task-5e90317e (DONE at sha 34baaf52): `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS`:39 still six keys; `DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS`:44 still five; `exactDesignRecord`:150; `decodeDesignRevision`:232 described as "The ONE decode of seat bytes in this slice"; `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS`:65 holds six codes; `designRefusal`:120 takes the CODE only. (c) RECORD THE MERGE-BASE BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground runs, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src/design` (task-5e90317e's own command; its baseline was `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 48 passed (48)`), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Any red here is FOREIGN and pre-existing - quote it now so step 5 can subtract it. (d) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/design/` and note peer dirt; never revert, stash or `git add -A` it.

THE SKIP SHAPE AND THE DISCRIMINATED DECODE. apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.ts only (259 lines - target <=250, hard cap 400; keep the addition tight). THE ARCHITECTURAL DECISION IS MADE HERE, NOT LEFT TO YOU - DoD-2 asks which arity rule was chosen, and the answer is TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, DISCRIMINATED ON THE PRESENCE OF `skipped`. Reasoning to carry into the completion record: adding `skipped` as a seventh REQUIRED key would make every existing six-key payload refuse, force every real design submission to carry `skipped: false` as wire noise, and break both fixtures and every arm task-5e90317e shipped. A separate skip shape breaks nothing and makes the half-skipped refusal fall out of exact arity instead of needing a bespoke consistency check. (1) Add `export const DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS = Object.freeze(["reason", "skipped"] as const)` - SORTED, like every roster in this file - and `export interface DesignSkip { readonly reason: string; readonly skipped: true }`. `reason` is bounded text via the existing `boundedDesignText`:144 (a skip is a product decision; an unexplained one is a decision nobody can review later). `skipped` must be the LITERAL `true`: a non-skip is expressed by submitting an actual design, never by `skipped: false`. (2) Widen the result type: `export type DesignRevisionOrSkip = DesignRevision | DesignSkip` and change `DesignRevisionResult`:117 to carry it. Add a type guard `export function isDesignSkip(value: DesignRevisionOrSkip): value is DesignSkip` - consumers (the surface row task-217f40b7, the mission row task-de059823) will narrow with it, so it must be exported, not inlined. (3) In `decodeDesignRevision`:232, discriminate BEFORE the existing arity check: if `Reflect.ownKeys(value)` contains "skipped", decode via `exactDesignRecord(value, DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS)` and require `skipped === true` plus `boundedDesignText(reason)`; otherwise fall through to the existing six-key path UNCHANGED. Do not touch the existing path's logic - it is guarded by 48 tests. (4) ADD NO NEW REFUSAL CODE. `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST already means "the exact-key roster refused the submitted revision" and covers every malformed case here. A new code would mean a new entry in the closed `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` map and a boundary-roster backfill for no gain - say in the record that you deliberately reused it.

CARRY THE UNION THROUGH THE RECORD. (1) apps/daemon/src/design/design-records.ts (118 lines): the import at :11 and `DesignRecord.revision` at :45 become `DesignRevisionOrSkip`. `DESIGN_RECORD_KEYS`:31 is UNCHANGED - `revision` is one key there, so the record's own arity does not move; say so explicitly in the step note, because a reader who assumes otherwise will go looking for a seventh record key that must not exist. Check `encodeDesignRecord`:58 and `decodeDesignRecordBytes`:87 - they round-trip through `decodeDesignRevision`, which step 2 already widened, so they should need no logic change; if either needs one, that is a signal the discrimination in step 2 is in the wrong place, so fix it there rather than special-casing here. (2) apps/daemon/src/design/design-store.ts (211 lines): probably NO EDIT. `submitDesignRevision`:130 assigns `revision: decoded.revision` and the type flows; `readDesignRevision`:189 returns `DesignReadResult`. VERIFY by `pnpm typecheck` rather than by editing - an unnecessary edit to this file is a diff a reviewer has to justify. If typecheck demands a change, keep it to the type annotation and nothing else. NOTE what this composition already gives you for free and record it: `submitDesignRevision` calls `readApprovedDesignContract` AFTER the decode, so a SKIP is subject to the same Gate-1-approved fence as a real design - you cannot skip a design for a goal whose contract was never approved. That is correct and matches the window the surface row offers the step in; assert it in step 4 rather than leaving it as an accident.

TESTS AND FIXTURES. (1) apps/daemon/src/design/design-test-fixtures.ts (57 lines): add `designSkipFixture()` returning `{ reason: "...", skipped: true }` beside the two existing revision fixtures. Read that file's header before editing - it supplies VALUES ONLY, no `expect`/`describe`/`it`, because a fixture that judged an outcome would be a second authority beside the one under test. Keep to that. (2) apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.test.ts (198 lines) - decode arms: a skip fixture round-trips and `isDesignSkip` narrows it true; THE SIX-KEY REVISION STILL ROUND-TRIPS UNCHANGED and `isDesignSkip` narrows it false (this is DoD-2's clause - it must assert the six-key outcome BY NAME, since the whole point of the two-arity choice is that nothing existing broke); `{skipped: true, reason, ...all six sections}` (8 keys) is REFUSED with code DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID and layer REQUEST asserted, both read from the result, not from a literal; `{skipped: false, reason}` is REFUSED with the same code and layer; `{skipped: true}` alone (1 key) is REFUSED; a `reason` that is empty, over MAX_DESIGN_TEXT (4096) or contains a NUL is REFUSED. (3) apps/daemon/src/design/design-store.test.ts (260 lines) - store arms against a REAL SqliteEventStore built by the production journey, the pattern the file already uses: submitting a skip lands a version and `readDesignRevision` answers it, narrowable by `isDesignSkip`; THE THREE STATES ARE DISTINGUISHABLE - no revision at all refuses DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT, a skip reads as a skip, a real design reads as a design (DoD-1 asks for all three because any two of them cannot tell the third apart); a skip submitted for a goal with NO approved Gate 1 contract is refused DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED @ CONTRACT_AUTHORITY (the fence step 3 noted comes free from the composition - pin it so a later refactor cannot quietly drop it); and a skip at v1 followed by a real design at v2 both live in history, which is the behaviour that lets an operator change their mind.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) MUTATION DRILLS, recorded in the step note. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST; every file in this plan is TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof for each - state EXPLICITLY that no untracked path was mutated and therefore no out-of-tree SHA256 backup was required, and prove each restore in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Three drills, restore and prove after each: (i) drop the `skipped === true` check so `{skipped: false, reason}` decodes as a skip - the DoD-3 arm must go RED naming DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID, not merely "threw"; (ii) replace `exactDesignRecord(value, DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS)` with a subset check so an 8-key half-skipped value is admitted - the half-skipped arm must go RED (this is the drill that proves exact arity is doing the work, per global rail 1); (iii) move the discrimination AFTER the six-key arity check so a skip never reaches its own path - the skip round-trip arm must go RED. Do NOT drill the pre-existing six-key path; task-5e90317e already drilled it with SHA256-proved restores and its arms are not this row's to re-grade. (b) GATES - standalone foreground runs, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting the `Test Files N passed` count line for each; an exit-0 leg with NO count line ran nothing and is not evidence: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src/design`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row and must not be quoted as such - vitest.config.ts:32 includes adapters/**, packages/**, tests/** and tools/**, no `apps/**`, so it runs zero tests against these files. Attribute any red by failing paths at HEAD minus failing paths at the step-1 merge-base baseline, intersected with apps/daemon/src/design/; that intersection must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red verbatim with its failing lines; never fabricate green. Named complete_task verification command: the `src/design` vitest leg above. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: a value carrying `skipped` inherited from a prototype rather than as an own key (`exactDesignRecord`:150 already rejects a non-`Object.prototype` prototype - confirm the discriminator uses `Reflect.ownKeys`, not `in`, or it inherits the hole); `skipped` present with a non-boolean value; a `reason` that is a String OBJECT rather than a primitive; two concurrent skip submissions at the same expectedVersion (the store fences with DESIGN_REVISION_CONFLICT - confirm, do not assume); a skip whose bytes are re-read through `decodeDesignRevisionBytes` and must come back as a skip, not as DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the arity rule chosen (TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, discriminated on `skipped`) and that the six-key path is provably unchanged, quoting that arm; that NO new refusal code was added and `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST was reused deliberately; the file roster you actually touched, with the note that this row's DESCRIPTION said four and the measured union of the key-roster grep and the `DesignRevision` type grep is five (six if design-store.ts needed a type annotation); and that the surface reading this marker is task-217f40b7 and the compiler mission stating it is task-de059823 - neither is this row's.

comments.content:
TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN DESCRIPTION, both made before planning. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. The plan (5 steps, 6 files) is built on the corrected facts; where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY.

## 1. The description says "exactly FOUR files". It is FIVE, maybe six.

I filed it after running `git grep -ln 'DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS|DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS|openDecisions'` — a grep of the KEY ROSTERS, not of the TYPE. `git grep -n 'DesignRevision\b'` additionally names:

    apps/daemon/src/design/design-records.ts:11   import { type DesignRevision }
    apps/daemon/src/design/design-records.ts:45   readonly revision: DesignRevision;

Measured union, all under `apps/daemon/src/design/`: design-contracts.ts, design-records.ts, design-contracts.test.ts, design-store.test.ts, design-test-fixtures.ts. design-store.ts is a maybe-sixth — `readDesignRevision`:189 returns `DesignReadResult` so the widened type should flow, and the plan tells the worker to settle that by typecheck rather than by editing it speculatively.

This is global rail 18 in miniature — grep the SHAPE, not the symbol — and it is recorded rather than quietly fixed so the next census does both greps. A file outside `apps/daemon/src/design/` remains a stop-and-report.

## 2. The description implies a seventh key. The plan chooses TWO ARITIES instead.

The description's hazard paragraph frames the choice as "either the new key is required on every revision, or the decode admits both arities" and leaves it open. Leaving the one architectural question in the row to the worker was my error; DoD-2 asks them to *state* the rule, not to *pick* it. **The rule is: two admitted arities, discriminated on the presence of `skipped`.**

    DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS = ["reason", "skipped"]        // skipped is the LITERAL true
    DesignRevisionOrSkip = DesignRevision | DesignSkip
    decodeDesignRevision: Reflect.ownKeys has "skipped"
                            ? exact arity over DESIGN_SKIP_KEYS
                            : the existing six-key path, UNCHANGED

Why, so it is not re-litigated: a seventh required key would make every existing six-key payload refuse (both fixtures plus every arm task-5e90317e shipped), force every REAL design submission to carry `skipped: false` as permanent wire noise, and make the design seat's brief teach a model to declare it is *not* skipping. Two arities break nothing, and the half-skipped refusal then falls out of exact arity rather than needing a bespoke consistency check — `{skipped:true, reason, ...six sections}` is 8 keys and fails both rosters.

`skipped` is the literal `true`, not a boolean: `skipped: false` would otherwise be a lawful revision carrying no design at all, which is the exact state DoD-3 requires be refused. A non-skip is expressed by submitting a design.

**No new refusal code.** `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST already reads "the exact-key section roster refused the submitted revision" and covers every case here. A new code means a new entry in the closed `DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS` map plus a boundary-roster backfill, for no diagnostic gain.

## One thing the composition gives free, and the plan pins it

`submitDesignRevision` (design-store.ts:130) decodes FIRST and calls `readApprovedDesignContract` SECOND — so a SKIP is subject to the same Gate-1-approved fence as a real design. You cannot skip the design for a goal whose contract was never approved, which is exactly the window task-217f40b7's surface offers the step in. Step 4 asserts it (`DESIGN_CONTRACT_NOT_APPROVED` @ `CONTRACT_AUTHORITY`) so a later refactor cannot quietly drop it.

`isDesignSkip` is EXPORTED on purpose: task-217f40b7 (surface) and task-de059823 (compiler mission) both narrow with it. Inlining the check would have each consumer re-implement the discriminator and drift.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE ARITY DECISION IS MADE AT PLAN TIME, not delegated. DoD-2 asks the worker to state which rule was chosen; leaving the CHOICE to them would have been an architect declining the one architectural question in the row.

CHOSEN - TWO ADMITTED ARITIES, discriminated on the presence of `skipped`. A skip is a 2-key record {reason, skipped:true}; a design is the existing 6-key record. `decodeDesignRevision` discriminates before its arity check and the existing six-key path is untouched.
REJECTED - `skipped` as a SEVENTH REQUIRED key on DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS. It is the shape the row description implied, and it is wrong on three counts: every existing six-key payload would refuse (both fixtures, every arm task-5e90317e shipped, and any caller already in flight); every REAL design submission would have to carry `skipped: false` as permanent wire noise; and the design seat's brief (task-de059823 step 2) would have to teach a seat to say it is not skipping, which is exactly the kind of sentence a model gets wrong. The half-skipped refusal would then need a bespoke consistency check instead of falling out of arity.
REJECTED - a separate SKIP EVENT TYPE on the same aggregate. Cleaner in the abstract, but a new event type needs a writer, and a writer needs a command kind - the measured three-row job (mem:decision-a-new-command-kind-is-a-three-row-job). The human's decision was explicitly to avoid a roster job.
REJECTED - a new refusal code such as DESIGN_SKIP_INVALID. `DESIGN_SHAPE_INVALID` @ REQUEST is already documented as "the exact-key section roster refused the submitted revision" and covers every case here. A new code means a new entry in the closed DESIGN_CODE_LAYERS map plus a boundary-roster backfill, for no diagnostic gain.
REJECTED - `skipped: boolean` rather than the literal `true`. `skipped: false` would then be a lawful revision carrying no design at all, which is precisely the half-skipped state DoD-3 requires be refused. A non-skip is expressed by submitting a design.
REJECTED - a bare {skipped: true} with no reason. A skip is a product decision; an unexplained one is unreviewable later, and `boundedDesignText` already exists to bound it at no cost.
